Linux distributions and kernels other than these two

limitations: Not clean machines in the plan's sense: both are the owner's long-lived hosts, not fresh installs. Neither has a Go or Rust toolchain, but both have other software (environment.hosts.<label>.other_software), including a C compiler. A static artifact does not use it; the check that it is not needed is that the binaries are static (file, ldd) and run under env -i with an empty PATH directory.

debian13-x64 was busy with the owner's workloads (load averages in per_host.debian13-x64.loadavg; the harness adds its own 'machine load was high' limitation when the load exceeds 0.75 x CPUs). Timing observations there are not comparable with an idle host. The harness ran under nice -n 10 on both hosts.
The harness venv on debian13-x64 was not created by pip (environment.hosts.debian13-x64.venv_method). pip's own install step was replaced by hash-checked extraction of the same two pinned wheels.
One run per candidate per host; timing observations are single samples.
Artifact provenance as in X1c: the X1b fix round's bytes, equal to the reviewers' rebuilds; a build of the committed candidate trees was not re-checked (no rebuild in this task).
linux-x64 is not a K13 verdict platform; these records are G02 practical-distribution evidence.
No independent review of this run.
